title: leptoskit.toml
description: Everything leptoskit needs to build, serve, and ship a project.

app.description: The application identity and platform defaults.

auth.description: Sign-in. Present when the app uses `leptoskit::auth`.

bundle.description:
What release builds ship: optimization, compression, and the size
budget.

db.description:
The database. `leptoskit db` is on when the table is present, even
empty.

extension.description:
The browser extension. Present when `extension` is one of the app's
platforms.

format.description:
How `leptoskit format` lays out markup. Omitted from serialized
configuration while it holds the defaults.

l10n.description:
Translations. Message generation is on when the table is present,
even empty.

lint.description:
What `leptoskit lint` checks. Omitted from serialized configuration
while it holds the defaults.

plugins.description: The leptos and leptoskit plugins activated for this project.

publish.description:
The stores `leptoskit publish` uploads to. Credentials never go
here.

router.description: File routes. The router is on when the table is present, even empty.

rpc.description:
The published RPC: what `leptoskit rpc` describes and generates
clients for.

schema_version.description:
Configuration contract version. Version 0 is unstable; breaking changes
are expected until version 1. Omitted versions are accepted for existing
projects; `leptoskit migrate` writes the current version.

default_platform.description:
The platform `leptoskit build` targets by default. `leptoskit dev` runs
every enabled platform this machine can run.

name.description: The package name; defaults to the directory name.

platforms.description:
Enabled application destinations. Each build selects one platform;
`leptoskit dev` runs all of them that this machine can run.

render.description:
How the web build renders: in the browser only, on the server with
full hydration, or on the server with interactive islands.

version.description: The semantic version of the app.

AttributeBraces.description: Whether the formatter keeps the braces around attribute values.

oneOf.description:
Remove braces the parser does not need: `class={name}` becomes
`class=name`, while `value={a > b}` keeps them.
Brace every value: `class=name` becomes `class={name}`.
Brace every value except literals: `id="a"` stays unbraced.
Keep each value as written.

AuthConfig.description:
Sign-in, through `leptoskit::auth`. Secrets are never written here:
each one is named by the environment variable that holds it.

absolute_days.description: Days a session lasts however often it's used.

access_minutes.description: Minutes a native app's access token works before it refreshes.

app_name.description: The app's name, as emails say it. Defaults to `app.name`.

client_ip_header.description:
The header a proxy in front of the server puts the client's IP
address in, such as `fly-client-ip`.

idp.description:
"Sign in with your app": other apps signing people in through this
one, with `leptoskit::idp`.

keys_env.description: The environment variable holding the server's keys.

mfa.description:
Who must use two-step verification: `optional` lets people choose,
and `required` asks everyone.

origin.description:
The site's origin, such as `https://myapp.com`. State-changing
requests from anywhere else are refused. Only `localhost` may use
plain `http`.

passwords.description:
Passwords: off unless turned on here. Needs `leptoskit_auth`'s
`password` feature.

providers.description:
Third-party sign-in providers, by ID: one of
[`AUTH_PROVIDER_KINDS`], such as `google` or `github`, or your own
name for any OpenID Connect issuer.

required_for.description:
Roles that must use two-step verification even when `mfa` is
`optional`, such as `["Admin"]`. The app says who has which role.

solana.description:
Solana wallets, which people link to their account with a signed
message. Needs `leptoskit_auth`'s `solana` feature and an `origin`.

AuthIdpConfig.description:
"Sign in with your app", through `leptoskit::idp`: an OAuth 2.1 and
OpenID Connect provider, so other apps sign people in with yours. The
scopes and claims it offers come from the app's code; this table holds
where its pages are and how long its tokens last.

access_minutes.description:
Minutes an access token lasts: revoking one reaches servers that only
check its signature after this long.

apps_per_person.description: The most apps one person may register in the developer portal.

audience.description:
What access tokens name as their audience: your API. Defaults to the
issuer.

consent_page.description: The page that asks people whether an app may sign them in.

developer_portal.description:
Lets signed-in people register apps of their own, for third-party
developers.

device_page.description: The page where people enter the code a CLI or a TV shows them.

dpop.description:
Takes DPoP proofs (RFC 9449), so apps can bind their tokens to a key
they hold, and a stolen token is useless without it.

dynamic_registration.description:
Lets apps register themselves at `/oauth/register` (RFC 7591), and
manage their registration with the token they get (RFC 7592).

issuer.description:
The issuer other apps discover the provider at, such as
`https://myapp.com`. Defaults to `auth.origin`.

refresh_days.description: Days an app stays signed in, however often it refreshes.

registration_token_env.description:
The environment variable holding the initial access token apps must
send to register, at least 32 characters. Without it, anyone may
register, at most 10 apps an hour from one address.

rsa_key_env.description:
The environment variable holding an RSA private key, as PEM, for apps
that need RS256 ID tokens. Without it every token is ES256.

sign_in_page.description: The page signed-out people sign in on before an app may sign them in.

signed_out_page.description: Where people go after an app signs them out, when it names nowhere.

signing_key_days.description: Days a signing key signs before the next one takes over.

AuthMailConfig.description:
How sign-in email is sent: over SMTP, or as a signed webhook to a URL
you control. With neither, development keeps email in a mailbox at
`/_leptoskit/mail`, and a release build refuses to start.

from.description: Who email comes from, such as `My App <hello@myapp.com>`.

smtp_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding an SMTP URL, such as
`smtps://user:password@smtp.example.com`.

webhook_secret_env.description: The environment variable holding the webhook's signing secret.

webhook_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the URL that receives each email as
a signed JSON webhook.

oneOf.description: People choose, and sensitive actions ask for step-up.
Everyone: until they set it up, a session may only do that.

AuthPasswordsConfig.description:
Passwords, as a way to sign in with the account's email address. Off by
default: passkeys and emailed codes do the same with less to steal.

breach_check.description:
Whether new passwords are checked against Have I Been Pwned's list
of breached passwords. Off by default, since it's a request to
another service; only the first 5 characters of the password's
SHA-1 hash are sent, never the password.

enabled.description: Whether people may set a password and sign in with it.

min_length.description:
The fewest characters a password may have: at least 8, at most 64.
The default, 15, is NIST SP 800-63B's for a password that's the only
factor; 8 is enough only where everyone has two-step verification.

AuthProviderConfig.description:
A third-party sign-in provider. Its secrets are named by the
environment variables that hold them.

api_version.description:
For `facebook`: the Graph API version, such as `v26.0`. Defaults to
the version leptoskit's definition was last checked against.

client_id_env.description:
The environment variable holding the OAuth client ID, or Apple's
Services ID.

client_secret_env.description:
The environment variable holding the client secret. An OpenID Connect
provider without one is a public client.

issuer.description:
For `oidc`: the issuer, whose discovery document names the
endpoints, such as `https://sso.example.com`. For `gitlab`: a
self-managed GitLab's address; defaults to `https://gitlab.com`.

key_id_env.description:
For `apple`: the environment variable holding the Sign in with Apple
key's ID.

kind.description:
What it is: one of [`AUTH_PROVIDER_KINDS`], such as `google`, or
`oidc`. Defaults to the provider's ID when that's a built-in one, and
to `oidc` otherwise.

name.description: What people see on its button, such as "Company SSO".

private_key_env.description:
For `apple`: the environment variable holding the key's `.p8`
contents.

scopes.description: The scopes to ask for, instead of the provider's defaults.

store_tokens.description:
Keeps the provider's access and refresh tokens, encrypted with the
server's keys, so the app can call its API on the person's behalf.
Off by default: signing in doesn't need them.

team_id_env.description: For `apple`: the environment variable holding the team ID.

tenant.description:
For `microsoft`: `common`, `organizations`, `consumers`, or a tenant
ID. Defaults to `common`.

AuthSolanaConfig.description:
Solana wallets. Linking a wallet is always on with the `solana`
feature; signing in with one is opt-in, here and for each wallet.

chain_id.description:
The cluster messages name, such as `mainnet` (the default),
`devnet`, or `testnet`.

sign_in.description:
Whether a wallet may sign in, once its owner turns that on for it.
A wallet signature is one factor, so two-step verification still
applies.

Browser.description: A family of browsers that share one extension package.

oneOf.description:
Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Arc, Vivaldi, and the other browsers built
on Chromium: one package for every Chromium store.
Firefox, signed by addons.mozilla.org.
Safari on macOS and iOS, shipped inside the app's own native build.

client_package.description:
The wasm client crate's package name. When unset, leptoskit detects
the workspace member producing a `cdylib` target.

features.description: Cargo features activated for app builds.

rustflags.description:
Extra rustc flags for the wasm client build. They merge with any
`target.wasm32-unknown-unknown.rustflags` in `.cargo/config.toml`. When
set, cargo ignores a `[build] rustflags` table for the wasm build, and
it ignores all of them when the `RUSTFLAGS` environment variable is set.

BundleConfig.description:
What a release build ships to the browser: how hard the client is
optimized, how its files are compressed, and how much it may weigh.

budget_kib.description:
The most the initial load may weigh, in KiB, brotli-compressed: every
script and wasm module the page fetches before any lazy chunk. Release
builds over it fail.

cargo_profile.description:
The cargo profile release builds compile the wasm client with, in
place of the one [`optimize`](Self::optimize) picks: the escape hatch
for full control from your `Cargo.toml`.

optimize.description: How hard release builds optimize the wasm client for size.

precompress.description:
Whether release builds write brotli (`.br`) and gzip (`.gz`) copies
next to every compressible file in the output, for servers to send
as-is.

split.description:
Whether the client is split with wasm-split: every `#[lazy]` function,
lazy route, and `#[island(lazy)]` moves into its own wasm chunk that
loads the first time it is needed, instead of with the page. Enabled
by default; clients without lazy code skip the splitting phase.

wasm_opt.description:
Whether release builds run `wasm-opt -Oz` over the wasm bundle.
Release builds fail with an install hint when this is on and
`wasm-opt` is not on the `PATH`.

ChromeStore.description:
An item in the Chrome Web Store, created once in its developer
dashboard.

publisher_id.description: The publisher's ID, from the developer dashboard's account page.

ClosingTags.description: How the formatter closes elements that have no children.

oneOf.description:
`
` becomes `
`. Void elements such as `
` are always self-closing.

`
` becomes `
`, except for void elements.
Keep each element as written.

allow_http.description:
Allows plaintext HTTP for an explicitly configured local development
registry. Native release builds always require HTTPS.

enabled.description: Whether code push is enabled for this project.

public_keys.description:
The ed25519 public keys, hex encoded, whose signed releases the app
installs. List the next key alongside the current one to rotate.

staging_dir.description: The local staging directory, relative to the app data directory.

ContentScript.description: An interface shown on other sites' pages.

browsers.description:
The families that get this script; every configured family when
omitted.

matches.description: The pages it runs on. Required for `manifest` scripts.

name.description:
The script's name, which the app injects or registers it by:
lowercase letters, digits, and dashes.

route.description: The app route the script's interface opens.

DbConfig.description:
The database: `leptoskit db` exports the tables declared in `crate`,
diffs them with the latest migration's snapshot, and writes new
migrations to `migrations`.

branch_databases.description:
Whether each git branch gets its own database on the development
Postgres, copied from the main branch's the first time it's used, so
switching branches never mixes their tables or rows. Off, every branch
shares the app's database.

crate.description:
The package whose `#[db::table]` structs are the schema. Defaults to
the app's name followed by `_db`, such as `my_app_db`.

dev_server.description:
Where `leptoskit dev` and `leptoskit db` find a Postgres database
when `url_env` isn't set.

dialect.description: The SQL dialect every migration is written for.

features.description:
The package features that compile its server side, so that its tables
export.

migrations.description: The migrations directory, relative to the project root.

policies.description: Who enforces the tables' access policies.

url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the database URL for `leptoskit db
migrate` and `leptoskit db status`.

watch.description: What `leptoskit dev` does when the tables change.

DbDevServer.description: The Postgres database development uses when `db.url_env` isn't set.

oneOf.description:
devenv's `services.postgres` when `devenv.nix` enables it, and the
embedded server otherwise.

devenv's `services.postgres`: run `leptoskit dev` inside `devenv
shell` while `devenv up` runs.

A Postgres that `leptoskit dev` runs itself, with its data in
`.leptoskit/db/postgres`. The first run downloads it once into
`~/.cache/leptoskit/postgresql`.
None: set `db.url_env` yourself.

DbDialect.description: The SQL dialect a project's migrations are written for.

oneOf.description: PostgreSQL, the default.
SQLite.

geopackage.description:
SQLite only: also keep GeoPackage's metadata tables, registering
each table's geometry column, so GIS tools such as QGIS open the
database file as layers. GeoPackage allows one geometry column per
table.

DbPolicies.description: Who enforces the tables' access policies.

oneOf.description:
The database layer adds each policy to every query it writes. Raw
SQL isn't filtered.

Postgres enforces them too, as row-level security that migrations
create from the same rules, so raw SQL is filtered as well. Rules read
the request through settings (`cx.setting::<G>()`), and the server
connects with `Db::with_row_security`. Postgres only.

DbWatch.description: What `leptoskit dev` does when the tables change.

oneOf.description:
Writes a migration for changes that keep every row and applies it to
the development database. Changes that would delete data write
nothing and say which command to run.

Applies changes straight to the development database, without
writing migrations, so the tables can change many times while an
idea takes shape. `leptoskit db migration create` then writes one
migration for all of them. Changes that would delete data are applied
only by `leptoskit db push --allow-destructive`.
Only prints what changed since the latest migration.
Ignores the tables.

EdgeStore.description: A product in Microsoft Partner Center, created once there.

product_id.description:
The product ID, from the product's Extension identity section. It
isn't the public Store ID.

events.description: The events that wake it, such as `runtime.message` and `alarms`.

description.description: What the shortcut does, as the browser's shortcut settings list it.

suggested_key.description: The keys suggested to the user, such as `Alt+Shift+C`.

ExtensionConfig.description: The extension: its surfaces, permissions, and per-browser settings.

background.description: The background worker: the events it wakes for.

browsers.description: The browser families to package for.

content_scripts.description: Interfaces shown on other sites' pages.

description.description:
One sentence about what the extension does, up to 132 characters,
which the Chrome Web Store allows.

name.description: The name stores and the browser show; defaults to `app.name`.

new_tab.description: A page that replaces the browser's new tab.

optional_host_permissions.description: Match patterns the extension asks for at run time.

permissions.description: Extension permissions, added to those the app's plugins need.

server.description:
The server the extension's API calls reach, such as
`https://api.example.com`. Its origin becomes a host permission.

side_panel.description:
The side panel (Chromium) or sidebar (Firefox). Safari has none, so
its package leaves it out.

ExtensionPage.description: A page surface: the route it opens.

browsers.description:
The families that get this page; every configured family when
omitted.

route.description: The app route the page opens, such as `/clip`.

FirefoxChannel.description: Where a Firefox add-on is distributed.

oneOf.description: Listed on addons.mozilla.org, after review.
Signed for you to distribute yourself.

data_collection.description:
The data the extension sends anywhere, in Firefox's categories, such
as `websiteContent` and `personallyIdentifyingInfo`; `["none"]` when
it sends nothing. addons.mozilla.org requires the declaration and
Firefox shows it at install.

id.description:
The add-on's ID, such as `commonplace@example.com`, which
addons.mozilla.org requires and keeps for good.

strict_min_version.description: The oldest Firefox that may install it; 121 by default.

FirefoxStore.description: An add-on on addons.mozilla.org. Its ID is `[extension.firefox].id`.

FormatConfig.description:
How `leptoskit format` lays out the markup inside `view!` macros.

Width and indentation are not set here: they come from the project's
`rustfmt.toml`, so markup and the Rust around it always agree.

attribute_braces.description: Whether braces around attribute values are kept or removed.

closing_tags.description: How elements without children are closed.

macros.description:
The macros whose markup is formatted, matched against the path written
at the call site: `view` matches `view! {}` but not `leptos::view! {}`.

rustfmt_toolchain.description:
The rustfmt toolchain that formats the Rust around and inside markup:
`nightly` by default, so unstable `rustfmt.toml` options apply,
`stable`, or any installed rustup toolchain name.

Inject.description: When a content script reaches a page.

oneOf.description:
Declared in the manifest, so it runs on every page its `matches`
cover, which needs host permission for each.

Packaged, but injected only when the app asks, for the tab the user
acted on. With `activeTab` it needs no host permission.
Packaged, and registered at run time for the sites the user allows.

L10nConfig.description:
Translations: `leptoskit l10n`, `dev` and `build` read the ARB files in
the locales directory and write the typed translations module.

dir.description:
The directory of ARB files, relative to the project root: one per
locale, named after its language tag, such as `en.arb` and
`pt-BR.arb`.

output.description:
The generated module, relative to the project root. Declare it where
it sits, such as `mod l10n;` in `src/lib.rs`.

template.description:
The locale whose file defines every message and the types of its
placeholders; the other files translate it.

LintConfig.description:
What `leptoskit lint` checks, from the `[lint]` table.

```toml
[lint]
markup = "view"
exclude = ["tests/fixtures/**"]

[lint.rules]
component_attribute = "deny"
```

clippy.description: Whether `leptoskit lint` runs `cargo clippy` beside its own rules.

exclude.description:
Paths the leptoskit rules skip, as globs relative to the directory of
this `leptoskit.toml`, such as `tests/fixtures/**`.

markup.description: How the project writes component trees.

rules.description: The level each rule reports at.

LintLevel.description: How a lint rule reports what it finds.

oneOf.description: Not checked.
Reported without failing the run, unless warnings are denied.
Reported, and fails the run.

LintRules.description: The level of each leptoskit lint rule.

children_last.description: Builder trees set their properties before their children.

color_literal.description:
Colors come from the theme rather than hand-written values. Off by
default.

component_attribute.description:
A capitalized function that returns a view is a component, so it
carries `#[component]`.

image_label.description: Every `Image` has an accessible name or is marked decorative.

markup_style.description: Component trees are written the way `markup` says.

redundant_view.description:
A `View` with no classes, props, or handlers does not wrap a single
child.

spacer_view.description:
Space between siblings comes from `gap-*` or `Spacer()`, not an empty
sized `View`.

MarkupStyle.description: How a project writes its component trees.

oneOf.description: Markup in `view!`: `view! { <Text class="p-4">"Hi"</Text> }`.
Builder calls: `Text("Hi").class("p-4")`.
Either, mixed freely.

MissingPlugins.description:
What a native build does with a selected plugin that has no
implementation on the platform being built.

oneOf.description:
Leave the plugin out and print a warning. Its calls fail with
`Unavailable`.
Stop the build.

android_certificates.description:
The SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificates that sign the Android
app, as `keytool -list` prints them (`AB:CD:…`, 32 bytes). With them,
`leptoskit::server` publishes `/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, and the
app's passkeys are accepted. List the upload key and the Play app
signing key when Google signs the release.

apple_team_id.description:
The Apple Developer team that signs the iOS and macOS apps, such as
`ABCDE12345`. With it, `leptoskit::server` publishes
`/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`, which lets the apps use
the site's passkeys and its sign-in return address.

missing-plugins.description:
What a build does when a selected plugin has no implementation the
platform's host can run. `warn` (the default) leaves it out with a
warning, so its calls fail with `Unavailable`; `error` stops the build.

package_id.description:
The reverse-domain application id used by platform shells, such as
`com.example.counter`.

It must have at least two dot-separated segments, each an ASCII letter
followed by ASCII letters or digits: the only form both iOS bundle ids
(no `_`) and Android package names (no `-`) accept. When unset it
defaults to [`default_package_id`] of the app name.

plugin-options.description:
Host-owned options for explicitly selected runtime plugins. These values
are embedded in native registration, never read from guest requests.

plugins.description:
Runtime plugins explicitly granted to the generated native app.
Each name must match metadata on a direct Cargo dependency.

targets.description: Legacy native target selection. New projects use `app.platforms`.

update_contract.description:
The app-owned native capability contract. Change this when a store
release changes plugin grants or native behavior incompatibly.

viewport_height.description: The initial viewport height for the headless layout pass.

viewport_width.description: The initial viewport width for the headless layout pass.

iOS.
Android.
HarmonyOS (ArkUI, packaged as a HAP).

Optimize.description: How hard a release build optimizes the wasm client for size.

oneOf.description:
Your `release` profile, then `wasm-opt -Oz`: small, and quick to

The browser build: wasm + SSR server.

PluginSpec.description:
One activated plugin.

Names without a `path` resolve against the built-in registry; a `path`
points at a plugin crate compiled into the tooling. Leptos plugins —
activated as cargo features on the app — are declared with `leptos = true`
and forwarded to the app build.

command.description:
The executable answering this plugin's hooks, for plugins that are
separate programs. Without it, `leptoskit-plugin-<name>` is looked up
on PATH.

leptos.description: Whether this is a leptos plugin, activated as an app cargo feature.

path.description: The path to a local plugin crate, when it is not a built-in.

PublishConfig.description: The stores an app is published to.

chrome.description: The Chrome Web Store, for the Chromium package.

edge.description: Microsoft Edge Add-ons, for the Chromium package.

RenderMode.description:
How a web build renders its interface.

The mode decides which cargo features each side of the build gets, which
follows the leptos convention: the server package is built with its `ssr`
feature and the wasm client with its `hydrate` feature.

oneOf.description:
Client-side rendering: the server only serves files, and the wasm
client renders the whole page. Neither side gets a mode feature. The
default, so a project opts into server rendering explicitly.

Server-side rendering with full hydration: the server renders every
page, and the client hydrates all of it.

Server-side rendering with islands: the server renders every page,
and the client hydrates only the `#[island]` components. Both sides
also get `leptos/islands`, so the wasm bundle carries nothing but the
islands.

RouterConfig.description:
File routes (legacy table; the router plugin is preferred): `leptoskit
plugin:router routes`, `dev` and `build` read the routes
directory and write the typed `Route` module beside it.

dir.description:
The routes directory, relative to the project root. The generated
module sits beside it with the same name, so `src/routes/` gets
`src/routes.rs`, which `mod routes;` finds.

RpcConfig.description:
The published RPC, as `leptoskit rpc` describes it and generates clients
for it.

Which functions are published is decided in code, with
`#[leptoskit_rpc::api]`; this section names the RPC, excludes functions by
pattern, and says where generated clients go.

description.description: A longer description for the OpenAPI document.

exclude.description:
Function-name globs (`*` and `?`) to leave out of everything generated,
in addition to `#[api(internal)]`.

include_internal.description:
Whether `#[api(internal)]` functions are generated too. Off for a
public package; on for an internal one.

servers.description:
The origins the RPC is served from. The first one is the default the
generated clients point at; none means the page's own origin.

targets.description:
What `leptoskit rpc generate` writes when no `--target` is given. Empty
means every target, into its default directory.

title.description: The RPC title; defaults to `<app.name> RPC`.

poll_seconds.description:
How often idle workers look for jobs that are due, in seconds, besides
being woken whenever a job is enqueued.

queues.description:
Queues with their own concurrency, by name, such as
`[rpc.jobs.queues.mail]`.

retention_days.description:
How many days finished and cancelled jobs are kept; 0 keeps them.
Failed jobs stay until someone retries them.

workers.description: How many jobs each instance runs at once.

concurrency.description:
How many of its jobs run at once, across every instance, so a
rate-limited service never sees more.

out.description:
The output directory, relative to the project root; each target has a
default under `clients/`.

package.description:
The package name: the npm package, the PyPI distribution, the Go
module, the cargo crate, or the Dart package.

scaffold.description:
How much regeneration writes: `create` (code always, scaffolding such
as manifests and READMEs only when missing — the default), `full`
(everything, overwriting), or `files` (code only; the package is the
user's to define).

server_url.description: The origin this client points at by default; overrides `rpc.servers`.

RunAt.description: When a declared content script runs, relative to the page loading.

oneOf.description: Before the page's own scripts.
After the document is parsed.
Once the page is idle: the browsers' default.

bundle_id_suffix.description:
Appended to `native.package_id` to make the Safari extension's bundle
identifier, which Apple requires to start with the app's.
